articles.title: “I was doing this celibacy thing”: Engaged New York Giants QB Jameis Winston gave up intimacy with then-fiancee Breion Allen for one solid reason
articles.summary: NFL News: Jameis Winston took the phrase “locked in” to a whole new level.The New York Giants veteran quarterback revealed on the New Heights podcast in January.
articles.body: Jameis Winston took the phrase “locked in” to a whole new level.The New York Giants veteran quarterback revealed on the New Heights podcast in January 2026 that he and his now-wife, then-fiancee, Breion Allen, chose to abstain from s*x during one of his Tampa Bay Buccaneers contract years [2019] because he wanted to stay completely and wholeheartedly focused on football.He just didn’t want any distractions. “I was doing this freakin’ celibacy thing,” Winston said, explaining his decision to temporarily put intimacy on the sidelines of his personal life.As shocking as it may sound, you read that right. While most players entering a contract year worry about statistics, film study, and staying healthy, Winston wanted to avoid one particular distraction. But did giving up s*x actually make him a better football player? The answer is a little more twisted than the locker-room myths might suggest.Does abstinence improve NFL players like Jameis Winston’s performance?Here is where science throws a flag on the much-debated play.There is no strong evidence that sexual abstinence directly makes an athlete stronger, faster or more explosive on the gridiron.A PubMed Central study deduced that sexual activity within 30 minutes to 24 hours before exercise did not majorly affect aerobic fitness, muscular endurance, or strength and power; in short, physical performance.So, contrary to one of sports’ oldest myths, NFL players do not naturally gain some mysterious physical advantage by avoiding s*x before games.Another systematic review similarly found that sexual activity the day before competition did not appear to negatively affect athletic performance.Simply put, Jameis Winston was not necessarily protecting some precious reserve of quarterback power by practicing celibacy for a year.The potential advantage was probably between the ears.How celibacy could help football players like Jameis Winston’s focusFor Winston, the biggest benefit may have been psychological.A contract year can bring enormous pressure to prove oneself. Every throw, mistake, and performance suddenly feels like it could gravely affect a player’s next paycheck. By intentionally removing one crucial part of his personal life, Winston may have created a stricter self-routine that kept his attention focused on football.That does not mean every NFL player should suddenly start mimicking Winston.Instead, his experience shows how athletes sometimes use personal sacrifices to reinforce self-discipline. If avoiding s*x helped Winston feel more focused, committed, and mentally prepared, then it may have benefited his overall preparation.The catchword, nevertheless, is focus.Any advantage would come from the strong mindset and stringent lifestyle surrounding the decision - not from abstinence itself magically boosting athletic ability on the gridiron.And Winston certainly made his contract-year strategy unforgettable. The New York Giants have since rewarded him with a two-year, $13 million extension through 2028, adding another intriguing chapter to the veteran quarterback’s unconventional NFL career.Can sexual abstinence have negative effects on athletes?There is another side to the intimacy story, too.Abstinence is not inherently harmful, but forcing yourself into it when you do not truly want to can probably give rise to other things like frustration, stress, or relationship tension. For an athlete, obsessing over the strict restriction could even become another distraction - the exact opposite reaction of what was wanted.There is also no proven scientific basis for the idea that athletes need to avoid s*x to preserve testosterone, strength, or aggression. Research has not consistently supported those long-standing, mythical locker-room beliefs.In the end, Winston’s celibacy experiment seems to have been about self-discipline rather than physiological benefit.If stepping away from s*x helped him eliminate distractions and feel mentally sharper during a crucial stage of his career, then it probably worked for him.But football players do not need to give up their s*x lives to perform at their very best on the gridiron.Winston simply chose a rather unforgettable way to say: when the contract was on the line, football came first. Before anything else.For 2019, the year that Jameis Winston prevented intimacy, he recorded - 5,109 passing yards, 33 touchdowns, and 30 interceptions in 16 games playing for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That was his career-best performance!Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 1 question for all 16 NFC teams entering 2026-2027 NFL season
articles.summary: 16 questions for 16 NFC teams entering the new NFL season.
articles.body:
The NFC successfully secured the Super Bowl title, with the Seattle Seahawks winning against the New England Patriots last year. The NFL is witnessing a wave of new coaching talent across various teams, and the NFC continues to showcase an impressive roster of dominant players. Here is one question facing every team entering the season.

Dec 21, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) warms up before the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images

Detroit Lions: Can the Lions stay healthy?

The Lions have a great roster with Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Penei Sewell, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and Aidan Hutchinson as their main core. The team's expectations should be high as their schedule gets a little easier, and it should be a great division race this season. The team had some injuries last year that hurt them.

Chicago Bears: Can the Bears execute back-to-back strong seasons?

The Chicago Bears shocked many NFL fans by getting to the playoffs and having a strong year. Caleb Williams took a big leap this past year, and the team has lots of weapons for him. Ben Johnson is one of the most creative coaches in the NFL, and the Bears should compete in this division

Minnesota Vikings: Can Kyler Murray fix the offense?

The Vikings were towards the bottom of the league in EPA/Pass and will need to be better in that category. Justin Jefferson is still one of the best in the league at the WR position, and the defense under Brian Flores last year was a solid unit. If Kyler Murray fixes this offense, this team will be better than people expect.

Green Bay Packers: Will the team stay healthy?

Micah Parsons will start on the PUP list, Josh Jacobs has off-field issues, Jayden Reed suffered an injury last year that kept him out for some time, and Tucker Kraft suffered a gruesome injury. Jordan Love and Matt Lafleur have shown resilience, managing to secure victories even with injuries affecting their roster. However, the competition within their division remains challenging. If Jordan Love and the team can maintain their performance while key players are sidelined, their prospects will improve significantly once Parsons and Jacobs return.

Jun 2, 2026; Woodland Hills, CA, USA; Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett (left) and coach Sean McVay react at press conference at Rams Practice Facility. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images

When you bring in Aaron Donald, that means the team wants to win another ring. The team is super good and will be the team to beat in the NFC. Trading for Myles Garrett is one thing, but adding Aaron Donald on top of it is another significant addition. The Rams are going to be very fun to watch with all of their new additions.

San Francisco 49ers: Can the team stay healthy?

For the 49ers, you have to give Kyle Shanahan lots of credit for last year. Multiple injuries on both sides of the field, and the team still made the playoffs and won a playoff game on the road versus the Philadelphia Eagles. When this team is healthy, they can compete with all teams in the NFC. Shanahan is incredible as an offensive mind, and Brock Purdy should have a great year. Lots of questions about the health of this team, but we shall see what they are capable of.

Seattle Seahawks: Can the Hawks repeat dominance?

First year under Mike Macdonald, they win a Super Bowl. The Rams upgraded their team, the 49ers are still a strong team, and the Cardinals are rebuilding. Why can't the Seahawks have another big year? They lost Kenneth Walker but replaced him with Jadrian Price.

Arizona Cardinals: Can Jerimayeh Love have a strong rookie year?

The division for the young running back Jerimayeh Love is not easy, and it will be interesting to see how Love does in his first season. It isn't easy to run the football when the offensive line is a question mark. The team will need to find ways to get him out in space.

Dec 14, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) carries the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Philadelphia Eagles: Can Jalen Hurts and the offense be on the same page?

The big question for the Philadelphia Eagles is their offense. Towards the middle of the pack offensively this past year. A brand-new offensive coordinator for the Eagles, Sean Mannion, will be a big reason why the Eagles either thrive or fail. Lots of pressure on Nick Sirianni this year and on the team. If a bad season occurs, don't be shocked if the Eagles have a new head coach.

Dallas Cowboys: Will the team be better defensively?

Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens are one of the best duos in the NFL offensively. Defensively, they drafted Caleb Downs, who will make an immediate impact on this team. Defensively, they had the least success on defense out of any unit in the NFL. Allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the NFC and the most passing yards, and allowed the 2nd most passing touchdowns too. Teams will be successful against the Cowboys if they can't stop their opponent.

New York Giants: Can the culture finally change in New York?

The New York Giants have made a significant move by hiring John Harbaugh. His reputation brings high expectations for a cultural shift within the team, and early signs indicate positive changes. The crucial question remains: will the Giants rise to compete and secure victories? Can he turn Jaxson Dart into a superstar? Some of those answers will unfold during the regular season, starting with their matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, where Harbaugh has historically excelled in opening weeks.

Washington Commanders: Will Jayden Daniels be able to stay healthy?

With Jayden Daniels, the offense thrives and can be a solid unit. But when he is not, the team is not going to perform well. Daniels was banged up last year and couldn't stay healthy. Can the offensive line hold up with Laremy Tunsil out with a major injury? Lots of questions for the Commanders this season that will need answers quickly.

Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) looks to pass during the third quarter against the New Orleans Saints at Bank of America Stadium. Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images

Carolina Panthers: Will we see another good year from Bryce Young?

The Panthers had a great year, and despite being eliminated in the playoffs last year, they put up a strong fight against the Los Angeles Rams. For Bryce Young, there was some inconsistency. He threw for 23 touchdowns while suffering 11 interceptions. He had the 20th-longest time to throw the football (2.70). If Young succeeds, this team can win the NFC South.

New Orleans Saints: Strong year or regression coming for Tyler Shough?

Tyler Shough showed lots of promise this season for the Saints despite dealing with some issues. The Saints' offensive line did not give him much time to throw, as he only had 2.54 seconds to throw the ball. He still finished with 10 touchdowns but turned the ball over 6 times. With improved offensive line play, those numbers should be able to be better. Chris Olave, Travis Ettiene, and Jordyn Tyson will all be reliable targets for him. Tyson is dealing with a hamstring injury, but when he is back, he will be an awesome target for Shough.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Will Baker Stay with the Team?

The Buccaneers are an interesting squad. They have some fun pieces like Emeka Egbuka, Baker Mayfield at QB, Chris Godwin, and Bucky Irving. Reuben Bain Jr, the rookie from Miami, should be a rookie of the year candidate. He has strong hands and the power to beat the tackles that he will go against. The Bucs may be able to contend, but if they don't, Baker Mayfield's days of being a Buccaneer are getting shorter.

Atlanta Falcons: Will this offense be successful?

The Falcons brought in Tua Tagovailoa and will be competing against Michael Penix Jr. Both QBs are good enough to create some offense. A brand-new head coach, Kevin Stefanski, enters the building. For Tua, health has been an issue, and Penix hasn't been able to be a consistent starter. This team has multiple weapons in Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. The offense should be run through Bijan, as he is one of the best offensive weapons in the NFL. It will be interesting how they utilize all of their pieces.

articles.title: Giants signing former Packers fourth-round pick to practice squad
articles.summary: The New York Giants are signing a former Green Bay Packers fourth-round pick to their practice squad.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are adding veteran free-agent defensive lineman Dean Lowry to their practice squad, reports ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Lowry, a veteran of nine NFL seasons, began his NFL career as a fourth-round pick of the Green Bay Packers out of Northwestern in 2016. After seven seasons with the Packers, Lowry played one year with the Minnesota Vikings before playing the last two seasons for the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Giants general manager Joe Schoen told reporters last week that the team would add a defensive lineman before the season opener this Sunday night against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium.

Lowry, who is returning from a torn ACL, has played in 132 NFL games with 85 starts. His best season was in 2021 when he recorded five sacks and had five defensed passes.

articles.title: Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy takes another turn as major NFL insider hints at new report before Patriots opener
articles.summary: NFL News: The Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy may not be finished yet. With the New England Patriots preparing for their season opener against the Seattl.
articles.body: The Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy may not be finished yet. With the New England Patriots preparing for their season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, fresh speculation has emerged that another report could surface before kickoff. NFL insider Albert Breer has pointed to continued interest in the story, while podcaster Tony Farmer has warned Patriots fans to “buckle up” as attention around the controversy builds again.Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy draws fresh attentionThe timing of the renewed speculation is significant. New England is days away from opening its campaign against Seattle, the same team that defeated the Patriots 29-13 in last season's championship game.Amid the preparations for that highly anticipated matchup, the controversy involving Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and former NFL reporter Dianna Russini has once again become a talking point.Breer discussed the situation during an appearance on the “Toucher and Hardy” podcast. Rather than predicting a specific report, he pointed to the sheer level of public interest and suggested that could encourage further reporting before the Patriots take the field."You guys saw the numbers on YouTube and on the podcast, and I saw the numbers at SI," Breer said. "For one reason or another, there is intense interest in this story. I think as long as there's that intense interest in the story, people are going to be pursuing it. It wouldn't surprise me if there was a story next week before the game on Wednesday."Farmer subsequently highlighted Breer's comments, suggesting that another development could create an unwanted distraction around the Patriots just as their new season gets underway."Buckle up: A new Dianna Russini article dropping before Wednesday's Patriots-Seahawks game? Listen as 98.5 radio personality suggests that a Patriots (S**t) storm may be imminent. Bert Breer also says it wouldn't surprise him if an article dropped before the Pats' Week 1 game."The comments do not confirm that a new report is coming. They instead reflect speculation surrounding a story that has continued to attract considerable attention.Mike Vrabel keeps focus on Patriots vs. SeahawksThe controversy first erupted after photographs of Russini and Vrabel at a private resort in Sedona became public. Additional images later emerged, including some dating back to 2021, intensifying scrutiny around their relationship.Russini ultimately left The Athletic. The publication then conducted an investigation that lasted several months before releasing its findings. According to the report, the relationship violated the company's standards. However, The Athletic's Director of Standards and Quality, Mike Semel, said the investigation found no evidence that Russini had shown favoritism toward Vrabel in her coverage of the Patriots.Vrabel has since made it clear that he does not intend to let the controversy dominate his attention.Asked about The Athletic's findings at a recent press conference, the Patriots coach declined to offer a detailed response."No, I don't have any reaction," Vrabel said. "We've moved on and focused on Seattle and focused on the Patriots and focused on getting better this week."That approach puts the spotlight back where Vrabel wants it: on football. articles.title: Tua Named Falcons QB1 Over Penix Jr. vs. Rodgers' Steelers, 6th New Week 1 Starter Since 2021
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons will have a new starter under center for a Week 1 matchup with Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers to begin the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons will have a new starter under center for a Week 1 matchup with Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers to begin the 2026 NFL season.

Atlanta named Tua Tagovailoa as its first-string quarterback over Michael Penix Jr. on Monday.

B/R NFL Scouting Dept's 2027 NFL Mock Draft Before 2026 Season

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN first reported the news. While not a total surprise, the revolving door under center continues for the organization.

Penix previously started nine games for the Falcons in 2025.

Tagovailoa signed a one-year contract with Atlanta in March after he was released by the Miami Dolphins, winning the Falcons' position battle while navigating through a back injury in training camp and overcoming early struggles in the preseason. He spent the first six years of his career as a member of the Dolphins.

Tagovailoa was selected by Miami with the No. 5 overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft.

He owned a record of 32-19 as a starter through his first four seasons in Miami, which included a 2023 campaign in which he threw for a league-leading 4,624 yards and earned a Pro Bowl nod.

Tagovailoa was limited to just 11 starts during the next year, as he missed time after suffering a concussion .

He followed it up with a disappointing 2025 campaign, completing 67.7 percent of his passes for just 2,660 yards and 20 touchdowns while getting picked off 15 times. Tagovailoa was benched for the Dolphins' final three games of the regular season.

The 28-year-old will look to bounce back with a change of scenery, while Penix is set to open the season as Atlanta's No. 2 quarterback.

Penix wasn't able to win the Falcons' starting job despite his prior experience in the role, as he's appeared in 14 games across his two years with the team.

It's worth noting that his 2025 season concluded earlier than expected after he suffered a torn ACL in Week 11 and he continued to recover from the injury in training camp. Penix wasn't fully cleared to practice until Aug. 22, eventually splitting first-team reps with Tagovailoa upon returning.

Atlanta is looking to end an eight-year playoff drought in 2026.

Tagovailoa and the Falcons are set to face the Steelers on Sept. 13, with kickoff at 1 p.m. ET.

But, hey, when in Rome. And the job compels us to give it a shot, whatever the outcome may be. The 2026 playoff trees and Super Bowl champions for each of the PFT writers appear below.

Fortunately, the results aren't part of our annual performance reviews. If they were, we'd all be fired. Starting with me, even though I own the place.

articles.title: Falcons choose Tua Tagovailoa over Michael Penix Jr. as Week 1 starter vs. Steelers
articles.summary: Atlanta turns to the veteran as Michael Penix Jr. continues working back from injury.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are naming Tua Tagovailoa their starting quarterback for Week 1 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the team announced Monday.

Tagovailoa won the job over Michael Penix Jr., who spent the preseason still recovering from his torn ACL that ended his 2025 campaign.

Head coach Kevin Stefanski may have tipped his hand earlier in the preseason, when Tagovailoa got the start in the team's first preseason game. When asked about his strategy, Stefanski said he prefers to play his starters in the first and third preseason games.

Tagovailoa played just one drive during the team's first game of the preseason. He finished 3-of-5 passing for 22 yards. In an otherwise mundane outing, the quarterback fumbled but recovered it.

Tagovailoa also played a drive in the team's third preseason game, going 7 of 8 with 95 yards.

The announcement comes on the heels of a training camp in which Tagovailoa got most of the work.

Penix was able to practice in 7-on-7 drills for the first two weeks and didn't get upgraded to full participation in 11-on-11 drills until the third week of the preseason.

This is Tagovailoa's first season with the Falcons. He began his career with the Miami Dolphins, but when the franchise went in a new direction and fired Mike McDaniel, Miami also opted to release Tagovailoa despite a massive dead cap hit .

The veteran QB played 14 games last season and went 6-8. He threw for 2,660 yards with 20 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. Tagovailoa completed 67.7% of his passes, his lowest percentage in a season since 2022.

Now that the Week 1 starter has been determined, the bigger question is whether Tagovailoa can keep the job moving forward. If Penix lost out on the starting role due to his health, how will the team handle the situation once he's ready to fully return to action?

Penix was the starting quarterback in 2025, ahead of veteran Kirk Cousins. He dealt with injuries throughout the season and played only nine games. Atlanta went 3-6 in those games as Penix finished with 1,982 yards, 9 touchdowns and 3 interceptions.
